title: How a thermostat works: feedback control
examples: How does a thermostat know when the room is too cold?
What is the difference between feedback and open-loop control?
Can you explain the role of the sensor in a thermostat?

explain.say: Today we learn about feedback control systems. These systems keep things steady.

draw.text: How a thermostat works: feedback control

explain.say: First we look at the set point. This is the desired temperature you want.
Next is the sensor. It measures the actual temperature in the room for us.
The controller takes the readings and compares them to the set point. It decides what to do.
Finally, negative feedback acts to reduce the error. It cools the difference down.
In real life, your body uses negative feedback too. When you get too hot, you sweat to cool down.

faq.q: What is the set point in a thermostat?
faq.a: The set point is simply the temperature you decide you want the room to be at. It is your target reading.
asks: What do I set the thermostat to?

faq.a: The sensor measures the current temperature and sends that reading to the controller. It acts like the eyes of the system.
asks: What is the job of the sensor?

faq.a: The controller compares the actual reading to the set point. It then sends a signal to fix any difference.
asks: How does the system know what to do?

faq.a: Negative feedback means the system automatically works to counteract or reduce any change. It brings things back to normal.

faq.q: Is this the same as a simple switch?
faq.a: No, a simple switch just turns something on or off. Feedback control constantly monitors and adjusts the level.
asks: Is it just on or off?

facts: A thermostat maintains a desired temperature range.
The sensor measures the actual environmental condition.
The controller compares the measurement to the set point.
Negative feedback automatically corrects deviations from the set point.

quiz.say: If the set point is 20 degrees and the sensor reads 15 degrees, what does the controller signal?
quiz.why: The controller sees a difference and signals the heater to reduce the gap.

wrong.0: Fans cool things down, which would make the difference worse.
wrong.1: If it does nothing, the temperature difference will remain too high.
wrong.2: Changing the set point is not the job of the controller right now.

quiz.say: Which component measures the actual temperature?
quiz.why: The sensor is specifically designed to take a measurement from the environment.

wrong.1: The controller makes the decision, it does not measure the temperature.
wrong.2: The set point is just the number you want, not the measuring tool.
wrong.3: Feedback is the action of sending the information back, not the measuring device itself.

quiz.say: When the room gets too hot, what action demonstrates negative feedback?
quiz.why: Negative feedback always works to oppose the change, so heat causes cooling.

wrong.0: A broken sensor would stop the system from working correctly.
wrong.2: Shutting off would let the temperature rise further, which is incorrect.
wrong.3: The set point is fixed; the system corrects the reading, not the target.
